notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

New games: Pokémon Colosseum, the PC port, built on this console. Add your own USA disc, press Build in its section on the web page (about 12 minutes on an OLED console) and it plays at 60 frames a second. Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus through SafeHouse, built the same way once your Sly Cooper disc is in the library (one and a half to two hours more on an original Switch). ProjectCane's Sly Cooper stays.

Xbox: a newer Xbox emulator, with fixes for games that stopped or closed on their own. System link over your network and Play Online keep working. When the emulator ends a game you return to SCCM Retro instead of RetroArch's menu, and the "Hash Generation Failed" message is gone. RetroArch's frame counter now shows the game's own rate, 30 in Halo 2; the game is not slower.

Fixes: Cemu no longer crashes at start once your otp.bin is added. x86_64 Linux programs start from the launcher. Handheld brightness is remembered across restarts. Remote Play's Login to PSN opens Sony's sign-in page instead of closing the app. A Bluetooth controller that drops during a game comes back in its own slot. The RAM tuner's "Save this setting and restart" works. Sly 2 finds your disc whatever its name or format. A PC game that crashes closes instead of freezing on screen, and the PC games report names where it crashed. An install that stopped at "Writing the partition table failed" carries on with the new SCCM Retro app.

Also: "Set every button to Nothing" in PC button mapping; Check for updates on the web page for Remote Play, YouTube, Stremio, Gen1Recomp and PokeMMO, and a Gen1Recomp you updated stays updated; encrypted 3DS games are turned away at import with the reason; the debug report keeps the Xbox emulator's own messages.

New and lightly tested: Colosseum and Sly Cooper were tried with USA discs and a virtual controller, not yet with real Joy-Cons or docked. Xbox was measured with Halo 2. The controller fix was tried with a simulated Pro Controller. Reports welcome.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
